transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-05 16:00 PST - Duration 47m - Recording on
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Samir (Redwood SE), Amir (Vela CTO), Lena (Vela Head Security), Priya (Vela Platform), Diego (Vela Compliance)

Summary: quick security review focused on encryption at rest and in transit, BYOK/HSM options, region residency guarantees, and operational playbook for key rotation and audit logs. Customer wants clear steps for onboarding HSM keys and validation for audits.

Topics: KMS/BYOK workflow, HSM integration options, key rotation and escrow, audit log retention, regional residency / eu-west-1 isolation, SOC2 artifacts and traceability.

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for making time, we'll do a run through of how Redwood handles encryption at rest and in transit, and then go into BYOK options. Maya will cover the ops playbook.
[00:18] Amir: Thanks Jordan, yeah main outcomes for us today are can we prove keys never leave our control, how traffic stays in our region, and what auditors will need. We also have a timeline, pilot in Q2 ideally.
[00:31] Maya: great, quick caveat, some of the names might get munged in the transcript, and there might be pauses. We'll try to be explicit about docs and links.
[00:38] Lena: good. I'd like us to focus on HSM onboarding and audit trails, specifically we use an HSM provider for BYOK, we need to know the TLS chain and whether Redwood retains any plaintext or unencrypted tokens.
[00:51] Samir: quick note, Redwood's private deploy supports a customer-managed KMS via BYOK. The control plane can be in Redwood or customer owned depending on private vs dedicated, but the two main patterns are keystore in KMS with envelope encryption or direct HSM sign ops.
[01:10] Priya: envelope encryption term is familiar but can you walk through request path? e g, model inference request, tokenization, cache, where are keys used?
[01:22] Maya: sure. Simplified path: request lands on endpoint, we allocate a short-lived session and fetch decryption key wrap from customer KMS, then runtime uses wrapped key to decrypt model layer keys in memory only, all KV caches are encrypted at rest, and TLS is used in transit. We do not persist unwrapped keys to disk. There is a short-lived in-memory plaintext key in the runtime process.
[01:46] Amir: in-memory only is good, but auditors often ask about crash dumps or core files. Do you have examples of mitigations?
[01:53] Jordan: yes we run processes with core dumps disabled, and we scrub memory on key release, we can share our hardening checklist. We'll attach the doc.
[02:05] Diego: also need statement on whether Redwood logs any customer plaintext or input text in cleartext in logs.
[02:11] Maya: by default we log metadata only, request IDs and latency; payloads are redacted in logs unless customers opt into deeper tracing for debugging. For pilot we recommend redaction on.
[02:26] Lena: ok. For BYOK we use an HSM vendor that supports Triple-A authentication and key attestation. We need a way to rotate keys and demonstrate lineage. How does Redwood surface rotation events?
[02:39] Samir: rotation model: customers can push a new key version in their KMS and then call a Redwood API to trigger rewrap, or we can poll. We persist key version metadata in our metadata store and every token issued has a key_version tag. Audit logs include key_version, operation, actor, timestamp.
[02:58] Priya: is key wrapping done in region? We cannot have key material leave eu-west-1 for EU customers.
[03:05] Maya: yes in private and dedicated we can ensure the KMS endpoint stays in the same region; the runtime instances live in the region and the key unwrapping happens inside those instances. For hosted customers we offer region pinning for EU only endpoints — traffic and key access are routed to eu-west-1.
[03:22] Amir: what's the fallback if capacity in eu-west-1 is saturated but request has EU data residency requirement?
[03:30] Jordan: Redwood has smart routing policies — for strict data residency we will not fallback to other regions, we'll queue or return capacity errors. For more lenient customers you can configure fallback to other EU regions or dedicated pools.
[03:45] Lena: auditors will want proof that fallback is disabled. Can you provide a signed config or snapshot?
[03:50] Maya: we can provide a signed config export and an S3-stored snapshot of routing rules; we'll add that to the next steps.
[03:58] Diego: retention of audit logs, our policy requires 7 years for certain records. What's Redwood retention and ability to export?
[04:06] Samir: default is 90 days in the product, but for enterprise/private we support configurable retention and long-term export to customer-managed S3/GCS with lifecycle rules. We can also stream logs to customer SIEM via secure connectors.
[04:20] Priya: perfect, we need long-term retention in our account. Also ensure logs are tamper-evident.
[04:26] Maya: we sign log bundles and provide hash chains; we can add attestation metadata. We'll demo that in the follow-up.
[04:37] Amir: HSM specifics: our vendor requires key import using an offline blanking ceremony, and we want to ensure the Redwood side doesn't see the unencrypted key. How is import performed?
[04:48] Samir: two ways: 1) Use KMS proxy where the customer keeps private key material in their HSM and Redwood holds only wrapped keys, or 2) export a wrapped key using vendor tooling and upload into Redwood's HSM connector in encrypted form. In both cases Redwood never sees unwrapped key material. We have documented steps for both flows.
[05:10] Lena: is there a way to get attestation from the runtime proving the key id used and that the operation happened inside an HSM boundary?
[05:18] Maya: yes, we emit attestation tokens — for some HSMs you can get an enclave quote or HSM attestation signature that is stored alongside the audit event. We include key_id, event_id, and attestation_blob.
[05:31] Diego: note, the compliance team will want the attestation to be verifiable offline. Is the blob verifiable with vendor public keys?
[05:37] Samir: yes vendor public keys are used, and we include the certificate chain with the event bundle.
[05:43] [06:00] Jordan: switching to encryption in transit, we use standard TLS 1.3 between clients and our edge, mutual TLS for private deployments, and mTLS for internal services depending on deployment.
[06:12] Priya: do you support custom CA for mTLS? We need to integrate with our internal PKI.
[06:18] Maya: yes for private deployments we can set up custom CA chains; we exchange CA certs during onboarding. For hosted we allow customer-managed client certs for mutual auth in dedicated/private lanes.
[06:30] Amir: question on ephemeral key lifetime, how long do session keys live?
[06:34] Samir: default session key life is short, ~5 minutes, but configurable per customer with max limits. Keys are rotated automatically by runtime.
[06:42] Lena: about key compromise, what's the incident response? We need revocation capability and keystore snapshot to show what was in use.
[06:51] Maya: incident playbook: we can revoke key versions, rewrap model encryption keys with new master key, and invalidate sessions. We provide a containment runbook and can run tabletop with your team.
[07:04] Amir: good. For auditors we'll need demonstrable evidence of past rotations and proof of no plaintext leakage. Can you provide example audit bundles?
[07:12] Jordan: yes we have sanitized audit bundles for SOC2 and some clients. We'll share a sample and a checklist of artifacts to collect.
[07:20] Diego: who on Redwood is responsible for signing off for production HSM onboarding? We want an operational contact.
[07:27] Jordan: Maya and Samir are the SE points and I'll be the commercial owner. For legal/compliance we have a dedicated security contact, I will include that email in the follow-up.
[07:36] Priya: operational detail - does the runtime write any temporary files that might persist keys? We need file system audit.
[07:43] Maya: runtime runs in ephemeral containers with tmpfs for sensitive memory and we mount only encrypted volumes. We also have a secure erase routine post-job.
[07:53] Priya: ok. Also curious on latency impact of external KMS calls — can you quantify?
[07:58] Samir: unwrapped key fetch adds 5-15ms depending on region and KMS latency, but we cache wrapped keys and reuse them within session TTL to reduce calls. For full numbers we'll run a short benchmark in your region.
[08:12] Amir: can Redwood provide a short benchmark showing 95th percentile latency with BYOK in eu-west-1?
[08:18] Jordan: yes that's in the next steps, Maya will coordinate with Priya.
[08:22] [08:30] Lena: one more question on legal chain: when we use Redwood hosted control plane but customer-managed KMS, who signs what in contract? We need liability boundaries spelled out.
[08:38] Jordan: typically responsibilities: customer retains key ownership and legal custody; Redwood provides runtime and controls for not persisting plaintext; contract includes KMS SLA and data residency terms. Legal will draft a clause. I'll loop in contracts.
[08:50] Amir: good. Also, can you support a no-ssh, no-shell-access operational mode for our instance?
[08:57] Maya: yes private deployments can be configured with no interactive shell, access via jump hosts only and strict RBAC using SSO.
[09:07] Priya: SSO — do you support SAML and OIDC? We run Okta.
[09:11] Samir: both SAML and OIDC, RBAC policies map to roles in the console and can be sync'd from Okta groups.
[09:20] Diego: final auditor ask: show us the chain of custody for a single inference event. Can you produce a timeline?
[09:28] Maya: yes we can generate a forensic bundle that includes request id, model version, key_version, attestation_blob, routing snapshot, and log hashes. We'll demo that in a follow-up.
[09:40] Jordan: ok wrapping up, quick recap of concrete deliverables.
[09:44] Maya: I'll prepare the KMS ops playbook with step-by-step for importing keys, rotation commands, how to trigger rewrap, and how to fetch audit bundles.
[09:53] Jordan: I'll send SOC2 excerpt, routing snapshot, and contact for security team.
[09:57] Priya: I'll send region list and desired retention policy.
[10:02] Lena: we'll review the attestation requirements and send key vendor details.
[10:07] Amir: timeline looks good — pilot Q2, follow up next week to set the benchmark window.
[10:12] Jordan: perfect. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with docs and set the bench window.

Questions noted during call: what auditors look for, where keys are unwrapped, whether Redwood logs payloads, fallback policies for region saturation, attestation verifiability, long-term audit retention, incident playbook and signed configs.

References/links mentioned: redwood KMS BYOK guide (link - to be shared), sample audit bundle (will be shared), SOC2 excerpt (will be shared).
